name: Evidence-first product design
description: Frame product design as an iterative practice that connects user evidence, product goals, constraints, designed behavior, and measured learning.

name: Figma workspace and file hygiene
description: Create, name, organize, share, and export Figma files using frames, layers, pages, and version-conscious professional habits.

name: Critique and design rationale
description: Give and receive specific critique, distinguish preference from evidence, and explain a design decision with observable reasoning.

name: Briefs, requirements, and scope
description: Interpret a product brief, identify ambiguity, ask useful questions, state assumptions, and define a feasible design scope.

name: Research questions and method choice
description: Turn product uncertainty into research questions and select a proportionate qualitative or quantitative method.

name: Research ethics, consent, and privacy
description: Recruit and work with participants ethically, obtain informed consent, minimize collected data, and document limitations.

name: Interviews and contextual observation
description: Plan and conduct neutral interviews or observation, take evidence-based notes, and avoid leading participants.

name: Surveys, sampling, and bias
description: Use surveys only when appropriate, write neutral questions, recognize sampling limits, and avoid overstating results.

name: Research synthesis and insights
description: Separate observations, patterns, findings, insights, and recommendations through traceable collaborative synthesis.

name: Problem framing and outcomes
description: Write evidence-backed problem statements, define outcome-oriented opportunities, and keep solutions separate from needs.

name: Journeys and task flows
description: Map an evidence-backed current journey and create task flows that expose decisions, branches, failure points, and recovery.

name: Information architecture and labeling
description: Organize content, name categories in user language, define navigation hierarchy, and explain the underlying mental model.

name: Card sorting and tree testing
description: Choose and run a bounded card sort or tree test, interpret limitations, and revise information architecture from evidence.

name: Sketching and concept divergence
description: Generate multiple low-cost concepts before convergence and compare them against evidence, constraints, and task outcomes.

name: Wireframing
description: Create low-fidelity wireframes that communicate hierarchy, content, navigation, and task behavior without premature polish.

name: Usability heuristics and evaluation
description: Apply established usability heuristics to identify, prioritize, and communicate interface risks without substituting inspection for user testing.

name: Interaction patterns and feedback
description: Design discoverable controls, navigation, feedback, confirmations, progressive disclosure, and reversible actions.

name: Forms and system states
description: Design forms, validation, errors, empty states, loading states, success states, permissions, and destructive actions as coherent flows.

name: Visual hierarchy and composition
description: Use scale, contrast, grouping, alignment, whitespace, density, and rhythm to communicate priority and relationships.

name: Typography systems
description: Choose readable type, establish a purposeful scale, control line length and spacing, and preserve hierarchy across viewports.

name: Color, contrast, and color independence
description: Build restrained semantic palettes, verify contrast, avoid color-only meaning, and document accessible color decisions.

name: Grids, spacing, imagery, and iconography
description: Apply coherent grids and spacing scales and select licensed imagery and recognizable icons that support content.

name: Responsive and multi-device design
description: Prioritize content and adapt layout, navigation, controls, and touch targets across narrow, medium, and wide contexts.

name: Figma auto layout and constraints
description: Build adaptable Figma frames with auto layout, resizing, constraints, and content stress tests.

name: Components, variants, and states
description: Create reusable components and variants whose names, properties, states, and overrides remain understandable.

name: Design-system foundations and tokens
description: Define a small system of foundations, semantic tokens, components, patterns, and usage guidance without premature over-systematization.

name: Interactive prototyping
description: Choose an appropriate fidelity and create task-focused prototype flows with meaningful feedback and realistic content.

name: Usability-test planning and moderation
description: Write neutral task scenarios, recruit representative participants, moderate without teaching, and capture observable behavior.

name: Findings, prioritization, and iteration
description: Convert test observations into traceable findings, prioritize by evidence and risk, and iterate without chasing every opinion.

name: WCAG-aware interface review
description: Apply relevant WCAG 2.2 principles to contrast, reflow, target size, focus, labels, errors, content, and non-text information.

name: Inclusive interaction and assistive-technology awareness
description: Anticipate keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, reduced-motion, cognitive, motor, hearing, and situational needs in design and testing.

name: Frontend implementation literacy
description: Explain how semantic HTML, CSS layout, breakpoints, components, content, and browser behavior constrain and enable a design.

name: Developer handoff and design QA
description: Prepare inspectable specifications, assets, states, responsive rules, acceptance notes, and constructive implementation QA.

name: Product goals, metrics, and tradeoffs
description: Connect design choices to user value, business constraints, feasibility, qualitative evidence, and bounded success measures.

name: Team workflow, tickets, and estimation
description: Work from tickets and briefs, decompose design work, estimate uncertainty, communicate progress, and collaborate asynchronously.

name: Stakeholder, client, and freelance communication
description: Set scope and revision boundaries, present uncertainty, negotiate feedback, document decisions, and hand over work professionally.

name: Responsible AI-assisted design
description: Use AI for bounded ideation, organization, critique, and repetitive work while protecting privacy and rejecting fabricated research or evidence.

name: Asset licensing and attribution
description: Select fonts, icons, images, and templates with appropriate licenses, attribution, privacy, and reuse discipline.

name: Portfolio case-study construction
description: Build concise case studies that connect problem, evidence, decisions, iterations, outcome, limitations, and learning without invented metrics.

name: Professional presentation and storytelling
description: Present a scoped design narrative, adapt detail to the audience, answer challenges honestly, and make evidence inspectable.

name: Independent end-to-end product design
description: Independently plan, execute, test, document, and present a reasonably scoped digital-product design under normal junior supervision.
